messages:
Maria: Heads-up: saw a 2-3x p99 tail on shared-gpu pool after a small burst from tenant=alpha yesterday ~14:23 UTC. Traces point to kernel selection flipping mid-request + a bunch of KV prefix miss spikes. Logs: `kernel: matmul_opt -> matmul_fallback` repeated a few times.
Sachin: Oof. Did this line up with the staged-batching rollout from last week? any deploys around that time?
Maria: Staged-batching went to 100% on pool-a two days ago. No infra deploys at 14:20. I attached the replay log below (trimmed).
Maria: ```
[14:23:12.432] req id=abc123 tenant=alpha seq=128 kernel_guess=matmul_opt exec_time=9.4ms
[14:23:12.441] req id=abc124 tenant=alpha seq=512 kernel_guess=matmul_fallback exec_time=34.1ms
[14:23:12.443] kernel_switch event req=abc125 old=matmul_opt new=matmul_fallback reason=cost_delta>0.35
[14:23:12.450] kv evict tenant=beta slot=0->tenant=alpha occupancy: beta=8% -> 2%
```
Zoe: That kv evict line is the thing. Alpha's burst warmed a hot path then ate most KV slots, which made other tenants miss and trigger costly recompute. We saw similar slot shadowing in a dev repro last quarter but this looks faster.
Li: Quick note: our kernel selector uses a 1s latency moving window + heuristic that biases toward recent low-latency microbenchmarks. If a burst of short-seq requests comes in, it can bias the selector to small-kernels; then a long-seq request forces a fallback and we pay the warmup cost.
Sachin: Could be a hysteresis/warmup problem. If selector flips too aggressively mid-batch, KV pinning + memory churn = p99 spike.
Maria: I replayed the exact trace locally with `rprof --replay trace/abc123.replay --concurrency 4` and saw the same kernel oscillation. Repro command and minimal diffs in case useful:
Maria: ```bash
# repro
rprof --replay trace/abc123.replay --seed 42 --profile-kernel-switches > /tmp/trace.out
# grep kernel_switch /tmp/trace.out | tail -n 20
```
perf-bot: Alert: perf-regression detected on pool-a 14:23 UTC. p99 increased from 18ms -> 62ms (4h window). Ticket: https://redwood/infra/PR-4567
Zoe: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) enforce a 5s selector pin after kernel decision per-tenant so it doesn't flip on the next request, 2) soft-cap KV slots per-tenant (like 40% max) with eviction priority, 3) short-term rate limit bursts >100qps for shared pool.
Li: For (1) we should be careful: pinning can harm long-tail throughput for legitimately diverse workloads. Maybe pin for the same short/long sequence class instead of blanket. e.g. pin keyed by (tenant, seq_class).
Sachin: Also add instrumentation: per-tenant `kernel_change_count`, `kv_evictions_by_tenant`, and `seq_class_histogram` to help verify hypothesis.
Maria: I've opened a debug-flag rollout to enable stable selector (no warmup bias) on pool-a only: https://redwood/ops/PR-7891 — will flip in 10m if CI/metrics look ok. Plan B is to revert staged-batching to canary.
ops-bot: ops-bot: Created rollback PR to revert staged-batching change on pool-a: https://redwood/ops/PR-7895. CI started.
Sachin: Action items: Maria to watch metrics and post p50/p95/p99 in 15m, Li to add kernel-change and kv-evict counters (quick patch), Zoe to draft soft-cap eviction policy, Ops to hold rollback if metrics stable.
Zoe: Long-term: scheduler should consider tenant-aware KV budgets + make kernel selector use sequence-class aware aggregation window to avoid warmup hysteresis.
Maria: Thanks. I'll keep updates here. If anything spikes again, ping @Sachin and I'll grab traces right away. :thumbsup:
